Stash for SQL-based backends

Source: R/MsBackendSql.R
MsBackendSqlStash.Rd

MsBackendOfflineSql backend classes defined in the MsBackendSql Bioconductor package can be stashed (or read from) plain text file or alabaster-based stash formats using the saveMsObject() and readMsObject() functions configuring the stash with a PlainTextParam or AlabasterParam parameter object. The Alabaster format is the preferred stash format.

Additional properties of the stash formats are described in detail in the sections below.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'MsBackendOfflineSql,PlainTextParam'
saveMsObject(object, param, consolidate = FALSE)

# S4 method for class 'MsBackendOfflineSql,PlainTextParam'
readMsObject(object, param, password = character(), ...)

# S4 method for class 'MsBackendOfflineSql'
saveObject(x, path, consolidate = FALSE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'MsBackendOfflineSql,AlabasterParam'
saveMsObject(object, param, consolidate = FALSE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'MsBackendOfflineSql,AlabasterParam'
readMsObject(object, param, password = character())

Arguments

object

An MsBackendOfflineSql object.

param

Either a PlainTextParam or AlabasterParam.

consolidate

logical(1) whether the database file should be copied into the stash folder. This is currently only supported for some database formats and systems. See notes section for details.

password

Optional character(1) with the password required to connect to the database. Passwords are never stored in a stash, thus, if required, the password to connect to the SQL database must be provided through this parameter.

...

Currently ignored.

x

For saveObject(): a MsBackendOfflineSql.

path

For saveObject() and readObject(): the path to the stash directory.

Value

readMsObject() returns a MsBackendSql::MsBackendOfflineSql object.

Note

For some SQL database systems it is possible to store also the database into the stash folder (by setting consolidate = TRUE in the saveMsObject() call). This is currently supported for:

  • SQLite-based databases (using the RSQLite package)

Alabaster format, AlabasterParam

saveMsObject() with an AlabasterParam() stores the backend to a stash folder in alabaster format. Individual components of the backend are stored using base functionality of the alabaster.base Bioconductor package into specific sub-folders within the main stash directory. These are:

  • dbinfo directory: contains a data.frame saved with alabaster.base with the database-specific information such as database name, host etc.

  • spectra_ids directory: contains an integer vector saved with alabaster.base with the IDs (indices) of the individual spectra.

The remaining directories hold the content of the MsBackendCached object the MsBackendOfflineSql extends (i.e., all locally cached data). Using parameter consolidate = TRUE will also store the database file within the folder (if supported).

In addition to the saveMsObject() and readMsObject() also the alabaster.base saveObject() and readObject() methods are directly supported.

Text-file format, PlainTextParam

saveMsObject() with a PlainTextParam stores the content of a MsBackendOfflineSql as text files into the stash folder. This creates two text files:

  • ms_backend_dbinfo.txt: a two-column tabulator delimited text file with columns "key" and "value" (first line being the header) with each row representing a key-value pair with the SQL database connection information. This includes "dbname" (the name of the database - for SQLite databases the SQLite database file name), "dbdriver" the database driver class (e.g. "RSQLite::SQLiteDriver" for SQLite databases), "user" with the database user, "host" with the host running the database and "port" with the respective port.

  • ms_backend_spectra_ids.txt: a single column text file (first row being the header of the table) with the spectrum identifiers (of type integer).

Remaining content, such as eventually present locally cached data, are stored through the saveMsObject() function of the parent MsBackendCached object (see MsBackendCachedStash for details).

Author

Johannes Rainer

Examples


## Create an example `Spectra` object
library(Spectra)
library(MsDataHub)

s <- Spectra(MsDataHub::X20171016_POOL_POS_1_105.134.mzML())
#> see ?MsDataHub and browseVignettes('MsDataHub') for documentation
#> loading from cache

## Store the full data into a SQLite SQL database
library(RSQLite)
library(MsBackendSql)
dbname <- tempfile()
s <- setBackend(s, MsBackendOfflineSql(), dbname = dbname, drv = SQLite())
#> Importing data ... 
#> 

#> [==========================================================] 1/1 (100%) in  0s
#> 
#> Creating indices 
#> .
#> .
#> .
#> .
#>  Done

## Stash the `Spectra` object to a temporary folder in alabaster format
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "spectra_sql")
saveMsObject(s, AlabasterParam(d))

## List the content of the SpectraStash
dir(d)
#> [1] "OBJECT"                        "_environment.json"            
#> [3] "backend"                       "metadata"                     
#> [5] "processing"                    "processing_chunk_size"        
#> [7] "processing_queue_variables"    "spectra_processing_queue.json"

## List the content of the MsBackendOfflineSql stash, which is located
## within the *backend* folder
dir(file.path(d, "backend"))
#> [1] "OBJECT"            "dbinfo"            "local_data"       
#> [4] "nspectra"          "spectra_ids"       "spectra_variables"

## Restore the object from the stash
res <- readMsObject(Spectra(), AlabasterParam(d))
res
#> MSn data (Spectra) with 931 spectra in a MsBackendOfflineSql backend:
#>       msLevel precursorMz  polarity
#>     <integer>   <numeric> <integer>
#> 1           1          NA         1
#> 2           1          NA         1
#> 3           1          NA         1
#> 4           1          NA         1
#> 5           1          NA         1
#> ...       ...         ...       ...
#> 927         1          NA         1
#> 928         1          NA         1
#> 929         1          NA         1
#> 930         1          NA         1
#> 931         1          NA         1
#>  ... 35 more variables/columns.
#>  Use  'spectraVariables' to list all of them.
#> Database: /tmp/RtmpFqcVt6/filea2a7c0e37c2
#> Processing:
#>  Switch backend from MsBackendMzR to MsBackendOfflineSql [Thu Oct 22 11:58:04 2026] 

## Verify a SQL backend is used
class(res@backend)
#> [1] "MsBackendOfflineSql"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "MsBackendSql"

## Repeat using the plain text file format. We need to first remove
## the previously generated stash, as overwriting an existing stash
## is not supported.
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)

## Use `consolidate = TRUE` to store also the database into the stash
saveMsObject(s, PlainTextParam(d), consolidate = TRUE)

## List the content of the SpectraStash
dir(d)
#> [1] "filea2a7c0e37c2"                  "ms_backend_data.txt"             
#> [3] "ms_backend_dbinfo.txt"            "ms_backend_nspectra.txt"         
#> [5] "ms_backend_spectra_ids.txt"       "ms_backend_spectra_variables.txt"
#> [7] "spectra_processing_queue.json"    "spectra_slots.txt"               

## Restore the object from the stash
res <- readMsObject(Spectra(), PlainTextParam(d))
res
#> MSn data (Spectra) with 931 spectra in a MsBackendOfflineSql backend:
#>       msLevel precursorMz  polarity
#>     <integer>   <numeric> <integer>
#> 1           1          NA         1
#> 2           1          NA         1
#> 3           1          NA         1
#> 4           1          NA         1
#> 5           1          NA         1
#> ...       ...         ...       ...
#> 927         1          NA         1
#> 928         1          NA         1
#> 929         1          NA         1
#> 930         1          NA         1
#> 931         1          NA         1
#>  ... 35 more variables/columns.
#>  Use  'spectraVariables' to list all of them.
#> Database: /tmp/RtmpFqcVt6/spectra_sql/filea2a7c0e37c2
#> Processing:
#>  Switch backend from MsBackendMzR to MsBackendOfflineSql [Thu Oct 22 11:58:04 2026] 

## Verify a SQL backend is used
class(res@backend)
#> [1] "MsBackendOfflineSql"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "MsBackendSql"
